result.comment: The plan has three stories: ship a Plan workflow and Markdown package matching Research, connect the three durable owner reviews, and connect checked publication with final approval and recovery. Your publication timing and whole-set review/rewind decisions are preserved. No owner questions remain. The proposed path stays opt-in while authentic host evidence is unavailable. Publication and readiness remain factory decisions; this proposal does not claim either. After publication and approval, use /implement build the three stories in dependency order.

plan.summary: Implement owner-reviewed Plan graphs with Research-style DOT, role and skill Markdown. Reuse existing graph, draft and publication machinery; review stories, engineering and acceptance, create complete issues after consistency, then obtain final approval on confirmed issues. Preserve whole-set revisions, durable replies, supersession, recovery, legacy compatibility and opt-in activation.

stories.title: Ship a Plan workflow package matching Research

user_story.want: a readable Plan workflow with the same Markdown organization as Research
user_story.benefit: understand and maintain the planning conversation without learning another structure
notes: Use one mode workflow, stage role documents and reusable skill/supporting documents. Keep existing execution available while the new path is connected.

acceptance_criteria.text: The application-owned Plan package mirrors Research's embedded organization: one editable plan.dot, stage role Markdown, and skills/<name>/SKILL.md with supporting Markdown. Roles explain stories, engineering, acceptance, consistency, publication and final review without introducing another catalog or installed instruction-tree regeneration.

The package declares stories → engineering → acceptance, explicit owner review gates, earliest-stage rewind routes, checked publication and post-publication final approval. All actions use registered lf_plan_* names; validation rejects unresolved actions, unsafe attributes and unbounded loops.

Plan capture retains the workflow, roles and selected skill/resource closure with immutable hashes; both provider deliveries resolve to those captured bytes. Missing resources, unsafe paths, cycles and resource-name collisions fail with actionable diagnostics.
Existing Research capture and graph validation remain compatible. This package alone does not enable default Plan graph admission, publish stories or change the mode.

Executed package/graph checks cover required ordering, control bounds, invalid resources/actions and both provider renderings using in-memory or temporary output. Evidence identifies the implementation snapshot and distinguishes offline rendering from authentic provider observation.

stories.title: Shape and approve stories through three durable Plan reviews

user_story.want: shape the whole story set, then its engineering details, then its acceptance criteria in separate reviews
user_story.benefit: resolve the problems and intended behavior before agreeing the finished technical plan
notes: Each stage covers the whole set, even when discussion concerns one story. A continuation request is not approval. Draft stories remain unpublished during discussion.

acceptance_criteria.text: Explicit opt-in admits new Plan graph executions using S1's captured package; default and active legacy executions retain their existing path and versions. Cold, resumed and fallback invocations use the same retained definitions even when shipped assets change; completing or pausing Plan never selects another mode.

Story shaping presents titles, descriptions, problems solved and intended benefits; engineering adds architecture, boundaries, dependencies and provisional tasks; acceptance adds prose success intent, canonical criteria, explicit completion signals and complete task mappings. Reviews display the whole set, current stage/revision, changes, questions and exact approval requested. No intermediate discussion or node completion creates story issues.

Only an authenticated owner response correlated to the displayed review, stage and current set revision can advance that gate. Wrong-owner, stale, duplicate or mismatched replies, silence, ordinary continuation, agent completion and input receipts cannot approve another revision or stage.

Meaningful additions/removals/splits/merges reopen story shaping; design/dependency changes reopen engineering; criteria-only changes reopen acceptance unless they change earlier intent. Clear whole-set approval at the earliest affected stage and every later stage while retaining content/history. Wording-only edits retain stage approvals only with a recorded comparison establishing unchanged meaning; uncertainty reopens review.

Persist stable draft/story identities, set/story revisions, stage content, dependencies, decisions, assumptions, unresolved questions, owner replies, review evidence and supersession links. Renames preserve identity; splits/merges create linked identities; removed drafts leave the active set. Restart or worker interruption around reply claim restores the originating review without skipping or double-advancing a gate.

Owner waits end the invocation and release worker capacity. Bounded-loop exhaustion retains drafts and explains the pause; explicit continuation starts a fresh bounded attempt without granting approval. Executed pure transition and real-store assembled tests cover stage gates, rewinds, reply authentication/correlation, restart, pinning and zero intermediate issue creation.

stories.title: Publish reviewed stories and approve the confirmed result

user_story.want: receive complete story issues after the three reviews and make the final decision on those published issues
user_story.benefit: approve the exact deliverable while interruptions or requested changes preserve the work and existing issue identities
notes: Acceptance-stage approval authorizes creation after consistency passes. Publication, final approval, readiness and implementation authorization remain distinct.

acceptance_criteria.text: Publication requires the same reviewed revision to have all three current whole-set approvals, a nonempty complete typed story set, resolved questions, valid criterion/task mappings and acyclic dependencies without missing or superseded targets. External dependencies resolve to retained issue identities. Reject invalid/stale content before remote writes. Acceptance approval authorizes this checked publication without another pre-publication approval gate.

Use the existing durable factory publisher to create/update complete issues and confirm the entire published set before final review. Surviving stories retain issue identity. Creation or an accepted input receipt alone cannot make graph Plan ready; readiness requires final owner approval of the exact confirmed set/revisions plus successful save. Preserve legacy readiness behavior.

Final rejection reopens the earliest affected review and all later reviews, repeats consistency checking and produces managed revisions before another final review. Any content change invalidates final approval. Competing/unconfirmed remote content cannot silently become the approved revision or be overwritten as if unchanged.

Post-publication rename preserves identity; removal/split/merge explicitly transitions active managed membership while retaining historical issue identities and supersession links. Removed/superseded stories leave the active publication, final-review and readiness set; surviving stories are updated rather than recreated. Preserve completed historical dependencies and do not introduce automatic deletion or closure policy.

On interrupted or uncertain create/update/attach/save, retain effect identities and receipts, reconcile before retry, and do not duplicate story issues. Final review remains unavailable until all publication effects are confirmed. Restart retains final-review correlation; stale/duplicate final replies cannot approve different issue revisions. Report input, publication, acceptance and readiness states honestly.

Executed assembled real-store publisher/daemon cases cover invalid pre-publication plans, partial/uncertain effects, reply loss/retry/restart, final rejection and republication, identity-preserving supersession, stale final approval, save failure and legacy compatibility; repository make check passes before engineering completion.

Document Plan opt-in, resume and activation prerequisites alongside Research guidance. Retain an evidence inventory distinguishing offline results from authentic Claude and Codex role/skill/helper invocation, same-run correction and authoritative receipt observations, including captured snapshot and host CLI versions. Missing authentic observations remain explicitly unverified and prevent default activation; do not claim them from synthetic tests or this planning run.
